name: Army Green
lede: Army Green is a dull olive associated with military uniforms and camouflage, recorded in the 2010 xkcd color-naming survey.

sections.title: A uniform's name, an undocumented coining
sections.body: The name joins "army" to a dull olive green, the shade long used for field uniforms and equipment because it blends into foliage [1]. ColorHub's library first catalogs the exact name from the 2010 xkcd crowd survey; which army, country or decade first used this specific wording as a formal color name is undocumented in the sources consulted [1]. Its nearest named look-alike is [[camo-green|Camo Green]], almost the same color, with [[mud-green|Mud Green]], [[navy-green|Navy Green]] and [[xander|Xander]] a little further off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this olive in 141 of 23,781 paintings (0.59 percent, as photographed), more common than 55 percent of named colors here [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.4 times the expected rate, most often as an accent, and is over-represented in American paintings (2.3 times expected) [3]. George Inness is its most devoted painter, using it in 5 of 45 works here, over seven times the baseline rate [3]. The earliest matching canvas dates to 1400, six centuries before the name was recorded; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first, and a look-alike hue, not proof the term is that old [3].
